 Unit 1: Introduction to chemistry
 1.1 Introduction
 Science is the systematic study of things in nature, the changes that
 are involved and the reasons for these changes. Our world is full
 of wonders of Science and Technology. As you continue to study
 Science, you will learn more about these. You might even become
 a great Scientist yourself and come up with your own interesting
 and useful discoveries.
 At primary school level, we learnt Science as a general subject.
 At secondary level, Science is divided into three main branches.
 These are Physics, Biology and Chemistry.
 SCIENCE
 BIOLOGY PHYSICS
 Biology is the study of
 living things. Physics is the study of
 CHEMISTRY objects, forces, light,
 heat, electricity, etc.
 Chemistry is the study of structure,
 composition of substances and the way
 they behave under different conditions.
 Fig.1.1 Branches of Science
 Physics, biology and chemistry can be applied in other subjects such
 as agriculture and home science.
 You have already learnt some aspects of Biology, Physics and Chemistry
 in primary school Science. In secondary school, you will build upon

 1.2 Review of chemistry topics covered at primary
 school level
 Matter
 In primary school Science, we learnt about matter. We learnt that matter
 is anything that has mass and occupies space. We can perform simple
 experiments to show that matter occupies space and has mass. The
 heavier an object is, the more mass it has. We also learnt that matter
 exists in three different forms namely:
 (i) Solids – e.g. stone, metal, wood.
 (ii) Liquids – e.g. water, kerosene, petrol.
 (iii) Gases – e.g. air
 Properties of matter
 In chemistry we study how matter behaves and how the state of
 a substance can be changed from one form into another under
 certain conditions. For instance, the volume of a gas can be reduced
 by increasing the pressure at a given temperature. A gas can be
 compressed, liquids can only be slightly compressed but the volume
 of a solid cannot be changed by pressure.
 Properties of the three states of matter
 • A solid has a definite shape and a fixed volume.
 • A liquid has no definite shape. It takes up the shape of the container
 in which it is put, but it has a fixed volume.

 The three types of matter will respond to certain changes. For example,

 Experiment 1.0
 To show that matter occupies space
 Apparatus and chemicals: Beaker, boiling tube, water.
 Procedure
 1. Fill the beaker or boiling tube completely with water.
 2. Add more water.
 What happens when you add excess water?
 Was your beaker initially empty?
 Liquids and solids fill a container. Once the container is completely
 full, if you add more of the liquid or solid it will spill over. Before the
 container is filled with a liquid or a solid, it is not as empty as it appears.
 It is usually full of air. It is only that we cannot see air. The liquid or
 solid displaces the air in the container! This experiment shows that
 liquids, solids and gases occupy space.

 Mixtures and their methods of separation
 You may have separated some mixtures at home or in school. For
 instance, you may have separated a mixture of maize and beans at
 home. Which method did you use? You may have also separated sand
 from water.
 How did you do this? How can you get clean water from muddy
 water?
 Maize and beans can be separated by hand-picking. Sand can be
 separated from water by pouring off the water. This method is called
 decantation. Clean water can be obtained from muddy water by
 filtering through a filter paper in a funnel. A piece of cloth can also be
 used. This method is called filtration.

 Drugs and drug abuse
 A drug is any natural or man-made substance that in some way changes
 the way in which our body works. Most medicines contain drugs.
 However, not all drugs are medicines.
 Over-the-counter (OTC) drugs
 There are some drugs which are bought from the Pharmacy shops
 without a doctor’s prescription. These are known as over-the-counter
 (OTC) drugs. The common OTC drugs include painkillers (such as
 aspirin and paracetamol), anti-acids and a variety of cold and flu
 remedies. These remedies that we buy for headache, stomach upset
 and other common ailments are drugs. We must use them responsibly.
 Medicine dosage
 Other drugs can only be obtained on prescription by a qualified doctor
 or health worker. These drugs need to be taken under more controlled
 medical supervision. One should follow the doctor’s instructions. Over-
 dosing or under-dosing oneself can lead to serious health problems.
 If you are taking prescription medication, consult your doctor or
 pharmacist before taking OTC medicines. Consumers who fail or
 disregard warnings on the labels of medicine package or inserts before
 they use OTC remedies do so at their own risk.
 Prescription
 It is very important that one strictly follows the doctors prescription.
 For example, Mburu got this prescription from a doctor who sent him
 to get the medicine from the pharmacy. He was instructed to take the
 medicine as follows : Amoxil 1 x 4 for 5 days
 : Paracetamol 2 x 3 for 3 days
 : Actifed syrup 2 tea spoons x 3 for 5 days
 A day is 24 hours. So, one must divide the hours of the day by the
 times the drugs are to be taken. For instance, amoxil should be taken
 after every 6 hours. If it is taken at 8.00 am in the morning, next dose
 should be at 2.00 pm in the afternoon then 8.00 pm in the evening
 and lastly 2.00 am at night. Paracetamol and actifed syrup should be
 taken after every 8 hours.

 Drugs like amoxil and other drugs can only work when they are
 taken as prescribed. When you forget to take them within the specified
 time, it is not advisable to take more or less to compensate. This will
 be drug abuse.
 Drug abuse
 Drug abuse is the use of a drug for any purpose other than that for
 which it is intended. Over-the-counter drugs such as pain-killers,
 anti-acids, headache tablets, malaria tablets and sleeping pills can be
 readily abused.
 Other drugs that are taken for various reasons and are readily abused
 include alcohol, tobacco, bhang, miraa (khat), heroin, cocaine, LSD,
 morphine, mandrax and many others. These drugs give a false feeling
 of well being. They have bad side effects and can be very damaging to
 one’s health or even lethal. It is also illegal in this country to possess,
 use or sell illegal drugs.
 Effects of misuse of drugs on the individual and family
 Medicinal drugs should be taken as per the prescription. Taking an over-
 dose or under-dose may lead to death or cause unnecessary expenses
 when other drugs are bought to correct the damage already caused.
 Smoking tobacco
 Data from research by World Health Organization (WHO) indicate that
 about one third of the global adult population are active smokers. It
 also estimates that half of the world’s children breathe air polluted by
 tobacco smoke, particularly at home. Each year tobacco kills about 4
 million people.
 Effects of tobacco on a smoker
 • Causes diseases such as bronchitis and tuberculosis to worsen.
 • Damages the lungs.
 • Discolours teeth.
 • Affects digestion of food.
 • It is an expensive habit: the money a smoker uses on cigarettes
 could be put into better use. Smoking in schools is not allowed.
 Students who are caught in the habit may be sent away from school.

 Effects of smoking on family and other people
 • Affects the family income leading to poverty.
 • Pollutes air, making non-smokers uncomfortable.
 Effects of alcoholism
 • Affects the brain and the nervous system.
 • Damages the liver ( liver cirrhosis).
 • Leads to poor health because alcoholics lose appetite.
 • Causes addiction.
 • Time meant for working is spent in drinking. An individual
 becomes unproductive and may lose his/her job. This affects
 the family and may lead to poverty. Students who drink may
 also be sent out of school.
 How alcoholism affects family members and the community
 • Alcoholics spend most of their money on alcohol and neglect
 the family leading to misery.
 • Drunk drivers easily cause accidents.
 • Drunk people are very unreasonable. They easily quarrel and fight.
 • Drunk people have weak morals, which leads to many activities
 that they would not do if they were sober, such as stealing and
 prostitution which may lead to one contracting HIV/AIDS. It
 also weakens a country’s economy and makes people poor.
 Drugs of dependency
 Drugs of dependency are those which contain substances that cause
 addiction, making the user very uncomfortable when they have not
 used them. These include alcohol, tobacco, bhang, miraa (khat), heroin,
 cocaine and many others
 Prevention of drug abuse
 We can prevent drug abuse by
 • proper use of all medicinal drugs.
 • never starting to use any illegal drugs.
 • keeping away from those who use or sell drugs.
 • using all our time productively by doing school work, games
 and sports or helping out at home and in the community.

 1.3 Chemistry and the society
 What is chemistry?
 Chemistry is the study of the structure and composition of substances
 and the way they behave under different conditions. For instance;
 what happens during the souring of milk; burning of wood, paper,
 kerosene and a candle; the decay of food and rusting of iron can all
 be explained in chemistry.
 The role of chemistry in society
 Look around you! Any material thing you can see or think of; be it
 furniture , cloth, paper, building materials, toothpaste, food and many
 more are the result of one chemical process or another. Chemistry
 has contributed a lot to modern technology. Through laboratory
 experiments, chemists have discovered new materials and the chemical
 processes to produce them in industries. As a result, our homes are
 made more comfortable today by the use of a variety of materials that
 were unknown when our great grandparents were young.
 Chemistry has contributed very much to our understanding of the
 material things which surround us.

 (d) When tests are carried out in hospital laboratories to diagnose some

 (f) The industrial manufacture of plastics, glass, cement, fabrics like

 (g) The processing of crude oil also requires chemistry.
 The importance of chemistry in our society is almost inexhaustible.

 1.4 The chemistry laboratory
 A laboratory is a room equipped with the necessary facilities for
 carrying out experiments in science. Chemistry experiments are done
 in order to learn about changes in substances. A laboratory is costly
 to build and to maintain. Therefore, careful management and care
 of laboratory equipment is essential. It requires the co-operation of
 everyone who uses the laboratory.
 Many chemicals are kept in the laboratory. Whereas some are
 harmless, others are poisonous. Some burn easily and can cause fire. Yet
 others have harmful effects on human beings or on the environment.
 All laboratory chemicals should therefore be handled with great care.
 Symbols or warning signs have been developed to indicate the dangers
 associated with chemicals and apparatus in the laboratory. Study
 appendix II which shows some of these symbols.
 We often use glassware in experiments in chemistry. Broken
 glassware can cause deep cuts. It is very important to prevent accidents
 in the laboratory.
 Fig.1.8: Students entering into the laboratory in an orderly manner
 Laboratory safety rules
 Keeping the laboratory safe is very important, hence, we have
 laboratory safety rules to observe while in the laboratory.
 • Do not enter the laboratory without the teacher’s permission.

 • Enter the laboratory in an orderly manner.
 • Do not rush as you enter the laboratory or scramble for the front
 bench.
 • Avoid unnecessary movement in the laboratory.
 • Do not do unauthorized experiments.
 • Do not taste any of the chemicals, even those that you think are
 harmless.
 • Do not tamper with electrical, gas or water fittings. Always turn
 off water taps and gas taps when not in use.
 • Do not smell gases directly. Hold the gas source about 15-20cm

 volatile liquids or solutions.
 • If chemicals get into contact with your clothes, skin, eyes or
 mouth, wash the affected area with plenty of water immediately.
 • In case of a burn or a cut, report the accident to the teacher or

 Some common apparatus in the laboratory
 Apparatus refers to the set of equipment used by chemists to do their
 work. Apparatus may be made of metal, wood, plastic or glass. Most
 apparatus used in chemistry experiments are made of glass. Can you
 suggest reasons for this?
 It is important to know the apparatus to choose and use when

 Here are some of the common laboratory apparatus.

 temperature and time.

 To investigate the parts of the Bunsen burner
 1. Unscrew the chimney of the Bunsen burner from the base plate and

 How does the air enter the chimney?
 By rotating the collar, the air supply can be regulated to obtain different
 types of flames.
 How to light the Bunsen burner
 Experiment 1.4
 Apparatus : Bunsen burner and a lighter.
 Procedure.
 1. Close the air hole and connect the burner to the gas tap using the
 rubber tubing.
 2. Light a match/wooden splint and hold it at the top of the chimney.
 3. Open the gas tap slowly half way then to fully open position. The
 gas should light. If it does not, switch off the gas tap then check to
 see that it is well connected to the gas supply before you try again.
 Ask for assistance from the teacher if you are still unable to light
 the Bunsen burner.

 Luminous flame

 It is therefore a luminous flame.
 Why does this flame give out light? When the air hole is closed, the
 gas is not fully burnt. There are unburnt carbon particles in the flame
 which give out soot. Other carbon particles become white hot and emit
 light. These white hot carbon particles are responsible for the luminous
 nature of the flame.

 A solution where water is the solvent
